prompt: I just finished writing this little rate-limiter package for our internal gateway (token bucket, refills on a ticker goroutine, has a Wait(ctx) and an Allow() and a Close()). Can you write the tests for it before I send the PR?
assertions: Tests live in an external test package (package limiter_test)
Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops

Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose only job is something the main goroutine could do directly (e.g. spawning a goroutine just to call Wait and be waited on); no gratuitous synctest.Wait; a hang is accepted as a valid failure mode rather than contorted around
Scenario grain: no per-symbol tests named exactly TestNew/TestAllow/TestWait/TestClose; at least one test composes several exported symbols as a user would
Names claim package properties in plain English without symbol/receiver stutter

Bodies are straight-line with hard-coded authoring-time expectations; the ONE sanctioned exception is panic-rejection cases via a table plus a recover helper whose failure message names the inputs and why they are invalid; no other case-generating loops or sub-test ceremony

Every test and example function carries a doc comment giving the rationale or contract clause in plain terms (why this test / why this mechanism when non-trivial), and none opens with its own function name
At least one runnable Example whose comment tells the same story the example shows (typical use, e.g. gating requests with Allow/Wait and Close on shutdown)
Contexts in tests come from t.Context() (Go 1.24) unless a stated reason requires otherwise
STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... passes with zero failures across all repetitions, and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes (flaky tests are contract failures)
